scientific_scope: Molecular neuroscience, neuroimmunology, translational pharmacology, disease modeling, and neural repair

subhypotheses.claim: Protein misfolding, aggregation, synaptic injury, and neuronal vulnerability are convergent but not identical mechanisms across Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease.
Pathology-targeting treatment can slow early Alzheimer’s decline but does not by itself establish cure or neuronal repair.
subhypotheses.evidence_class: mechanistic review plus randomized clinical trial
subhypotheses.writing_mode: direct for studied population; no extrapolation

subhypotheses.claim: Neuroinflammation and microglial state are context-dependent therapeutic targets.
Human iPSC models can test patient-genotype-linked autophagy and neuronal phenotypes but incompletely model aging and whole-brain disease.
Drug repurposing accelerates candidate selection but requires brain exposure, target engagement, and disease-stage-specific validation.
Neuronal replacement is a repair module whose efficacy depends on disease-environment control and safe circuit integration.

prohibited_inferences: A treatment that slows decline is a cure.
A single common pathway means one drug treats all neurodegenerative diseases.
An iPSC phenotype proves clinical efficacy.
Repurposed approval proves efficacy or brain target engagement.
Stem-cell transplantation is safe or curative without integration and long-term follow-up.
